criteria.title: Money flows in scope: authorize, capture, refund, payout, reconcile

levels.0: Only 'charge the card', with no refunds, payouts or ledger.
levels.1: Covers charging, refunds and payouts, but never separates authorization from capture or leaves reconciliation out.
levels.2: Authorize at checkout, capture on shipment, void on cancel, refunds, a double-entry ledger for every movement, daily seller payouts and daily reconciliation; fraud, 3-D Secure and multi-currency explicitly out of scope.

levels.0: Generic targets (fast, highly available) with nothing about money.
levels.1: Says 'no double charges' but does not rank correctness against availability or mention durability of acknowledged payments.
levels.2: Charged exactly once, money never created or destroyed, RPO 0 for acknowledged payments, no raw card data, and states that when an outcome is uncertain the system stops and finds out rather than staying available.

criteria.title: Payment rate, PSP budget and database load

levels.0: No numbers, or numbers without derivation.
levels.1: Derives 116/s and a 10x peak of about 1,160/s but never compares them with the PSP rate limit or sizes the database.
levels.2: 116/s average and 1,157/s peak; PSP calls checked against 2,000/s per PSP including failover (58%) and throttled captures (78%); 2 transactions per checkout giving about 4,244 ops/s on one primary at ρ ≈ 0.53; 60M ledger entries and 22 GB a day.

levels.1: Sizes the API fleet from QPS but ignores that each authorization holds a connection for about 800 ms.
levels.2: 48 instances (16 per zone) from 9,260/s at 500 per instance with a zone lost; about 980 concurrent PSP calls by Little's law, rising to over 11,000 if the PSP slows to the timeout, which motivates per-PSP bulkheads.

criteria.title: Checkout API with idempotency and honest status codes

levels.0: A POST /pay with a card number in the body.
levels.1: Uses a PSP token and an idempotency key, but has no answer for an unknown outcome or uses floating-point amounts.
levels.2: PSP-tokenized card, integer minor units, Idempotency-Key with stored response and 422 on a changed body, 402 for declines, 202 'processing' for unknown outcomes with a status endpoint, and signature-verified, deduplicated webhooks.

criteria.title: Payments, idempotency records, ledger and outbox in one ACID store

levels.0: A payments table with a status and amount column only.
levels.1: Has a ledger table, but entries are mutable, idempotency keys live in a cache, or the store choice is not justified.
levels.2: Payment with versioned state and transition history, idempotency records in the same database, immutable ledger entries grouped into balanced transactions, an outbox table, and Postgres with a synchronous replica chosen for multi-row transactions and constraints.

criteria.title: Checkout flow around the PSP call

levels.0: Calls the PSP inside a database transaction, or writes to the DB only after the PSP answers.
levels.1: Records intent before the PSP call, but publishes events with a dual write or has no path for captures and webhooks.
levels.2: Pre-call transaction, PSP call with our payment_id as idempotency key and reference and no transaction open, post-call compare-and-set with outbox; asynchronous capture workers, webhook handling through the state machine, and a latency budget that meets 3 s p99.

criteria.title: Exactly-once effects and the unknown outcome

levels.0: Treats a timeout as a failure and lets the buyer retry.
levels.1: Uses idempotency keys at our API but not toward the PSP, or retries with a fresh key.
levels.2: Idempotency at all three hops, an unknown state resolved by status queries and webhooks with backoff, voids for late authorizations, and never failing over an in-flight payment to the second PSP.

criteria.title: State machine, outbox and saga framing

levels.0: A free-form status column set by whoever arrives last.
levels.1: Draws states but transitions are unconditional updates, or events are published after commit.
levels.2: Allowed-transition table with compare-and-set, terminal states that late webhooks cannot leave, transactional outbox compared with CDC, 2PC and event sourcing, and void/refund as saga compensations.

levels.0: Balances updated in place with no entries.
levels.1: Balanced entries, but corrections edit rows or every payment locks the platform's fee account.
levels.2: Balanced immutable entries with a worked example, reversing transactions for corrections, no UPDATE/DELETE privilege, materialised seller balances, and platform hot accounts handled by asynchronous balances or sub-accounts.

levels.1: Mentions a daily comparison but has no matching key or no plan for each kind of break.
levels.2: Matches by our reference sent to the PSP, classifies breaks (missing on either side, amount, bank deposit) with a resolution for each, aims for over 99.9% automatic matches, and adds hourly API-based checks for unknown payments.

levels.1: Covers database failover and zone loss but not PSP degradation, or misidentifies what breaks first at 10x.
levels.2: A PSP-degradation timeline (bulkhead fills, unknowns, breaker opens, new payments to B, unknowns resolved, reconciliation confirms); at 10x names the PSP rate limit first, then sharding by payment_id with balances as projections.

levels.1: Generic trade-offs not tied to payments.
levels.2: Each key choice (auth then capture, keys in the payment DB, unknown state, two PSPs, Postgres, outbox, immutable ledger, asynchronous platform balances) with the alternative and why it lost here.
